chunks: Beware that piety is like trained horses
on whom the riders have been placed with the reins in their hands, so that they would take the riders to Heaven
There is right and wrong and there are followers for each
If wrong dominates, it has (always) in the past been so, and if truth goes down that too has often occurred
It seldom happens that a thing that lags behind comes forward
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor of piety as a horse in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this sermon delivered upon his arrival in Medina, Imam Ali (AS) employs the metaphor of 'trained horses' to illustrate how piety (Taqwa) serves as the reliable means of transport to Paradise, emphasizing its practical utility in navigating life's trials. He contrasts the historical prevalence of falsehood with the enduring resilience of truth, offering a theological perspective on the temporary nature of injustice and the ultimate certainty of divine victory, a theme deeply resonant in Shia eschatology.
